story: Spinning around: Please don't – Common problems with spin locks
text: As always: use standard libraries, profile, then write your own if the data indicates it's necessary. The following is an interesting talk where the author used a spinlock to speed up a real-time physics solver significantly. Dennis Gustafsson – Parallelizing the physics solver – BSC 2025 [VIDEO]

story: Futurelock: A subtle risk in async Rust
text: From my understanding this talk describes how he implemented a solution for a similar problem [VIDEO] I'm saying if you're not writing multi-threaded code everyday, use a library. It can use atomics/locks but you shouldn't use it directly. If the library is designed well it'd be impossible to deadlock.
